title: Prototype Chain Check
description: Predict own vs inherited property lookups via Object.create, Object.assign, in, and Object.hasOwn.

questions.explanation: `greet` lives on `parent`, not directly on `child`. `Object.hasOwn` only reports own properties, so it returns `false`.

questions.prompt: Using the same `child`, what does `"greet" in child` print?
questions.explanation: The `in` operator checks the entire prototype chain, so it finds `greet` on `parent` and reports `true`.

options.text: `true` — assign copies properties directly onto the target

questions.explanation: `Object.assign(target, source)` copies `source`'s properties as own properties onto `target`. `b` becomes an own property of `child`.

questions.prompt: For the same `child` (prototype has `a`, own property `b`), what does `Object.hasOwn(child, "a")` print?
questions.explanation: `a` is only reachable through the prototype (`{ a: 1 }`), not copied onto `child` — so it is not an own property.

questions.prompt: What does `"c" in child` print when `child` has no `c` on itself or on its prototype?
questions.explanation: If a key is not found anywhere in the prototype chain (own or inherited), `in` reports `false`.

questions.prompt: Which pair of checks correctly distinguishes "own" from "inherited" for a given key on an object?

options.text: `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` for own, and `key in obj` (when hasOwn is false) for inherited

questions.explanation: Check `Object.hasOwn` first for own properties; if that is false but `key in obj` is true, the property is inherited from the prototype chain.
